# Conformance and support matrix

What the SelfAuth Flask (Python) reference implementation is tested against, which compliance level each
store reaches, and what is not supported. Specification version: **0.1**.

A generator that runs is not a conformant adapter. A level is claimed only
when the cases for it pass in CI and every non-case requirement has a recorded
sign-off with evidence (`conformance/adapters/flask.json`).

## Compliance levels

| Level | Needs | Cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core compliant | all core cases pass; every automated check for core requirements (adapter, schema, migration tests) is signed off | 71 |
| Authorization compliant | core, plus the authorization cases and the authorization checks | 18 |
| Production-profile compliant | all cases, plus every review, documentation and static-analysis item signed off | 1 |

The suite has 90 cases in total.

## Result

| Store | Published level |
| --- | --- |
| memory | Authorization compliant |
| mongodb | Authorization compliant |
| mysql | Authorization compliant |
| postgresql | Authorization compliant |
| sqlite | Authorization compliant |

**No independent security audit has been done.** Production-profile status is self-assessed from the sign-offs below. An outside review is required before 1.0.

CI runs the whole suite against the in-memory store and against PostgreSQL, and fails if either measures below its published level.

## Support matrix

| Kind | Supported | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| backend | `gin` | Flask 3 + Python 3.11+ (a Python port of the core) |
| database | `postgresql` | PostgreSQL via psycopg 3 (the same migration SQL as the TypeScript apps; a small migration runner in Python) (store `postgresql`) |
| database | `mysql` | MySQL 8 or MariaDB via PyMySQL (the schema derived from the PostgreSQL reference; a small migration runner in Python) (store `mysql`) |
| database | `sqlite` | SQLite via sqlite3 (standard library): one file on one host, no server (the schema derived from the PostgreSQL reference) (store `sqlite`) |
| database | `mongodb` | MongoDB 6+ via PyMongo (the same collections and documents as the TypeScript store; indexes, not migrations) (store `mongodb`) |
| database | `memory` | In-memory (development and tests only) (store `memory`) |
| frontend | `none` | API only |
| frontend | `vue` | Vue 3 (generated as client/ next to the Flask server in server/; browser-tested against the Flask server) |
| frontend | `react` | React (generated as client/ next to the Flask server in server/; browser-tested against the Flask server) |

Not supported yet: see [Known limitations](#known-limitations).

## Known limitations

- Every database is claimed at authorization level, not production: the production profile has not been reviewed for the Flask adapter. MySQL, SQLite and MongoDB are held to the same 90 cases as PostgreSQL, on a real server (SQLite needs none).
- `selfauth add` does not work on existing Python projects (new projects only). A Vue or React frontend is generated as `client/` next to the Flask server in `server/`.
- The in-memory store loses data on restart and keeps rate limits per process. It is capped at authorization level and is not for production.
- The migration runner does not detect destructive statements in a way that blocks (it is reviewed by `selfauth db plan`): read every migration before applying it.
- Three implementations of the core now exist. The conformance suite detects drift in the behaviour it covers; behaviour outside the cases is covered by the Python unit tests and review. Known differences (trusted proxies as false, a hop count or a list of addresses, simple case folding of email addresses, trailing slashes) are listed in apps/playground-flask/README.md.
- Email and password only. No OAuth, social login, MFA or passkeys (optional capabilities, not built).
- The mailer is a stub: you must implement create_mailer before production, and the server refuses to start in production without one.
- Production-profile status is not claimed for Flask: the adapter has had no review except its author's. The sign-offs below are self-assessed, and no independent security audit has been done.
- SQLite is one file on one host: its rate limits are not shared across application instances. Use PostgreSQL, MySQL or MongoDB to run several instances.
- On MySQL a migration file that fails halfway leaves its earlier statements in place (MySQL commits DDL as it goes): restore from a backup, fix the file and run it again. MongoDB has no migrations; `migrate up` creates the missing indexes and never drops one.

## Sign-offs

Requirements proven by something other than a conformance case, and how.

| Requirement | Method | Finding | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IDENT-DELETE-005 | documentation | docs/data-retention.md lists what deletion clears, deletes, revokes and keeps, how long, and how to purge it; checked against delete_account in the Python core (app/auth/service.py) and the migration SQL, which is the same schema as the TypeScript apps. | `docs/data-retention.md` |
| AUTHN-REG-003 | adapter-test | The store contract test makes the role link fail and asserts no user or credential remains; it runs against the in-memory and SQLite stores always, and PostgreSQL, MySQL and MongoDB when their server is configured (CI), where creation is one transaction or one document. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_store.py`, `apps/playground-flask/tests/support.py`, `apps/playground-flask/app/store/sqlstore.py`, `apps/playground-flask/app/store/mongostore.py` |
| AUTHN-LOGIN-003 | adapter-test | A test counts Argon2 evaluations: a login for an account that does not exist costs exactly as many as a login with a wrong password. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_service.py` |
| AUTHN-LOGIN-003 | code-review | Login calls verify_dummy on the no-user path and has no early return before password verification; the dummy hash is computed when the hasher is built, so the first unknown login costs no more than the rest. | `apps/playground-flask/app/auth/service.py` |
| AUTHN-REG-010 | adapter-test | A test counts Argon2 evaluations: registering an address that already has an account costs the same as a new one. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_service.py` |
| AUTHN-REG-010 | code-review | Register hashes the password before looking the email up, so every path costs the same. | `apps/playground-flask/app/auth/service.py` |
| AUTHZ-CORE-002 | code-review | The example route is guarded and tested anonymously; routes on auth.protected(...) deny every request that no guard allows (tested). Unlike the TypeScript apps there is no test that fails on any unguarded route in application code: that remains a review item. | `apps/playground-flask/app/routes.py`, `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_routes.py`, `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_hardening.py`, `apps/playground-flask/app/flask_auth.py` |
| AUTHZ-PERM-001 | schema-test | Config validation rejects malformed permission names. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_config.py` |
| AUTHZ-PERM-002 | schema-test | Config validation rejects project permissions using the reserved 'auth.' prefix. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_config.py` |
| AUTHZ-PERM-004 | schema-test | Config validation rejects roles that reference undefined permissions. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_config.py` |
| AUTHZ-PERM-004 | adapter-test | require_permission with an undefined permission raises when the route is defined. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_hardening.py` |

| SEC-HASH-001 | code-review | Hashing is argon2-cffi's low-level Argon2id (hash_secret_raw, Type.ID); there is no hand-written implementation, and verification compares in constant time (hmac.compare_digest). | `apps/playground-flask/app/auth/password.py`, `docs/adr/0028-flask-backend.md` |
| SEC-HASH-006 | adapter-test | A test shows the number of concurrent Argon2 runs is capped by a bounded semaphore, so a burst of requests cannot exhaust memory; the server's thread pool is bounded too. | `apps/playground-flask/tests/test_service.py` |

## Reproduce

```bash
pnpm build
pnpm --filter @selfauth/conformance coverage:report
pnpm --filter @selfauth/playground-flask test        # runs every case; set TEST_DATABASE_URL for PostgreSQL
```
